text:
## Abstract  
This study quantified the publicly available Escherichia coli (taxid 562) data in two widely used NCBI-linked repositories that capture distinct layers of experimental information: (i) processed gene‐expression studies in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and (ii) raw high-throughput sequencing runs in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA, accessed via BRC Analytics). Using programmatic queries, we identified 1,929 GEO Series (GSE) records annotated with “Escherichia coli” as the organism, representing expression-profiling studies, and 551,679 E. coli sequencing runs deposited in ENA. These figures provide an up-to-date estimate of the breadth of transcriptomic and raw sequencing resources for this model organism, highlighting the extensive volume of data available for secondary analysis, meta-studies and method development.

## I. Introduction  
Background.  Escherichia coli is a key bacterial model organism and a major pathogen, making its publicly available omics datasets critical for basic research, biotechnology and antimicrobial-resistance surveillance.  
Literature Review.  No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap.  A consolidated, current count of E. coli expression studies and raw sequencing runs across major public repositories was not available from a single source.  
Objective & Hypothesis.  We sought to enumerate (1) GEO Series capturing E. coli expression experiments and (2) ENA raw sequencing runs for taxid 562, hypothesising that both repositories hold extensive but distinct datasets.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design.  One repository was queried for each data type: GEO for expression studies (Series-level records) and ENA (via the BRC Analytics proxy) for raw sequencing runs.  
Materials.  
• GEO — queried with functions.geo_search  
• ENA (via BRC Analytics) — queried with functions.brc_ena_runs  
Procedures.  
1. GEO expression studies  
   • Tool: `geo_search`  
   • Arguments: organism="Escherichia coli"; entry_type="gse"; max_results=1  
   • Purpose: return `total_count` of matching Series (GSE) records.  
2. ENA raw sequencing runs  
   • Tool: `brc_ena_runs`  
   • Arguments: taxonomy_id="562"; limit=1; offset=0  
   • Purpose: obtain `total_in_ena`, the total number of runs for E. coli.  
Statistical Analysis.  No statistical transformation was required. Counts were taken directly from the `total_count` (GEO) and `total_in_ena` (ENA) fields returned by the APIs.

## III. Results  
Data Presentation.  

Table 1. Publicly available E. coli omics datasets (24 September 2023).  
| Data type | Repository queried | Count | Field source | Query parameters | Date retrieved |  
|-----------|-------------------|-------|--------------|------------------|---------------|  
| Expression profiling Series (GSE) | GEO | 1,929 | `total_count` | organism="Escherichia coli"; entry_type="gse" | 2023-09-24 |  
| Raw sequencing runs | ENA | 551,679 | `total_in_ena` | taxonomy_id = 562 | 2023-09-24 |  

Findings. GEO indexes 1,929 E. coli expression Series. ENA contains 551,679 sequencing runs annotated with taxid 562.

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The repositories collectively hold nearly two thousand processed expression studies and over half a million raw sequencing runs, indicating rich resources for systems-level and genomic analyses of E. coli.  
Context. The disparity (three orders of magnitude) reflects how a single expression study can encompass multiple samples but is archived as one Series, whereas each biological or technical run is individually accessioned in ENA.  
Limitations.  
• GEO query relied on organism annotation and “gse” filter; misannotation could under- or overcount.  
• ENA count aggregates every run for taxid 562, including diverse strains and study types; it does not equate to unique isolates or experiments.  
• No assessment of data quality, completeness or redundancy was performed.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. Public archives currently provide extensive E. coli omics data: >1,900 expression studies and >550,000 raw sequencing runs. Future work could stratify these resources by strain, assay type, or study design to guide targeted re-analyses and benchmark efforts. Integration with additional repositories (e.g., SRA metadata, proteomics databases) would offer a more comprehensive landscape.

## References  
[1] GEO. Query: "Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND "gse"[Filter]. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?db=gds&term=%22Escherichia%20coli%22%5BOrganism%5D%20AND%20%22gse%22%5BFilter%5D&retmax=1  
[2] ENA via BRC Analytics. Taxonomy id 562 runs. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562?limit=1  

## Acknowledgments  
We thank the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) for GEO and ENA data services and BRC Analytics for providing the ENA proxy API.
